brief: A 3D-printed PLA spacer block. The base is a 30 mm square plate 4 mm thick. A 12 mm diameter post 10 mm tall stands in the middle of it, with a 2 mm fillet where the post meets the plate. A 5 mm hole runs all the way through the post and the plate. Two 3 mm mounting holes pass all the way through the plate, 20 mm apart. It must weigh no more than 8 g. It carries no load - it is a printed spacer, so there is no load case.

notes: dropped REQ_SF_BEARING: the brief states this part carries no load, so there is no load case to take a margin against and nothing could have computed one
added REQ_MASS at_most 8 g: the brief states it as a limit and the whole-part mass slot was left empty, so nothing would have checked the one number a printed part is most often judged on

added REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_X and REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_Y at 30 mm: the brief calls the part square or round at its largest stated size, and nothing in the requirement set measured the part's size at all. A dimension parameter is declared just as truthfully by a plate 30 by 12 as by a plate 30 by 30, and one was: sixteen claims, every one green, and the plate was 30 by 12.

added REQ_HOLES_5MM: the brief states 1 open hole of 5 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.

added REQ_HOLES_3MM: the brief states 2 open holes of 3 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.

answer.rationale: The brief describes the part as square or round at its largest stated size, which states both extents.
